Concentration-round first-touch (triage seat): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task S, routed `domain:devx` (a `scripts/check-*.mjs` gate over test infrastructure — the devx face of this repo).

Queued despite zero live instances because the class is invisible by construction (the one occurrence was caught only by an ablation leg, and 577 live specifiers have no other guard) and the check is already written and measured cheap (~1s, no build). Scope ruled: relative `vi.mock`/`vi.doMock` specifiers only, **error** not warning (the card is right — no legitimate reason exists to mock a nonexistent path); bare-specifier coverage deferred until a real instance shows (different resolver, different failure mode — don't build it speculatively). Self-test both ways: a planted unresolvable specifier must fail, the 577 real ones must pass. Precedent lineage #4347 noted.

## PM claim + dispatch order — R27

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-5646-inert-vi-mock-gate`.

### Ruling: **build the gate.** And answer the card's three open questions as follows.

The card is right that this is the same family as #4347 — a declaration pointing at nothing, reported as a pass — one layer down. It is also right that it is not a cleanup card: **0 unresolvable specifiers today**, so nothing is broken and the whole value is preventing the next one.

⭐ That fact is also the trap. **A gate that is green at rest is indistinguishable from a gate that does nothing**, and this one will be green on the day it lands. Its ablation is therefore not a formality — it is the only evidence the gate exists at all.

The three questions, decided:

1. **Bare specifiers (`vi.mock('@object-ui/…')`)** — ⛔ **out of scope.** Resolving them needs the workspace map rather than the filesystem, which is a different check with a different failure mode. File a follow-up if you think it is worth one; do not widen this gate into it.
2. **Error or warning** — **error.** There is no legitimate reason to mock a path that does not exist, and a warning in a repo this size is a line nobody reads.
3. **`vi.mock(import('…'))`** — cover it if the same regex already matches it, since that is free. ⛔ Do not invent handling for a form no call site uses; say in the report that the population for it is currently zero.

### ⭐ The positive control is not synthetic — use the real historical instance

PR #5645 wrote `vi.mock('../runtime-config', …)` from `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/`, one `..` short of the real `'../../runtime-config'`. The suite **passed**, and passed even when the subject was reverted to the broken shape the suite was written to catch.

**Reconstruct that exact specifier and prove the gate reds on it.** A gate for this defect that cannot catch the one instance we know occurred is not worth landing. ⛔ Do not settle for a made-up `'./nope'`.

Then the discriminating half, which matters just as much:

⭐ **Prove it does NOT red on the neighbours that made the bug invisible.** In that same file, `'../AiUsageIndicator'` (one level) and `'../../hooks/surfaceAgent'` (two levels) are **both correct**, because the targets sit at different depths. A resolver that got depth wrong would flag those and be deleted by the first person it annoyed.

### Resolution must match the repo's real specifier style

The card's scan already establishes what is needed, and it is more than a bare `existsSync`:

- try the bare path **plus** `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` / `.jsx` / `.mjs` / `.cjs`
- try the `/index.*` forms
- **strip a trailing `.js`**, because `src/` uses NodeNext specifier style throughout

⛔ Get any of these wrong and the gate reds on hundreds of correct call sites. Reproduce the card's census as your baseline — **1807 test files, 577 relative specifiers, 0 unresolvable** — and ⚠️ **re-derive it rather than quoting it**; that measurement is days old and this repo moves fast.

### ⛔ Non-vacuity, stated as the thing I will check hardest

- **The population must refuse to collapse.** If the walk finds zero test files or zero specifiers, the gate must **fail**, not pass. A scan that silently finds nothing reads as coverage — that is exactly the defect this gate exists to prevent, one level up, and PR #6195 landed that discipline tonight as `expect(tracked.length).toBeGreaterThan(1000)`. Follow that shape.
- Report the census in the verdict line so a future reader sees the population, not just "OK".
- Mutations proven on disk by anchored counts, never by an editor's exit code; restore via `git checkout HEAD --` followed by the explicit path, proven with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

The card says the scan runs in about a second with no build, install or vitest run — so it belongs in the **cheap-gate tier**. ⚠️ Confirm that yourself and say where you wired it; if it needs an install to run, it is in the wrong tier and the pre-install import-graph gate (#6148 / PR #6159) now governs what a pre-install step may import.

### Scope

A new `scripts/check-*.mjs` in the existing family, its test, and the workflow wiring. ⛔ Do not fix any test file — there is nothing to fix, and if your re-derivation finds an unresolvable specifier that is a **finding**: report it, and only then decide with me whether it lands here.

Root vitest only (objectui#3378). ⚠️ Derive the gate list you run from `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` rather than from this order — I have named a script file instead of an npm script twice tonight and been corrected both times.

## PM review — ACCEPTED. PR #6198 armed. ⭐ And it is the first new gate to land under #6187's contract, which it followed correctly.

Reviewed against a pinned ref. 15 green, 0 failures, 8 running — and **"Inert vi.mock Specifier Check" is already reporting green on its own PR, in 10 seconds.**

### ⭐ It satisfies the derived merge_group floor that landed an hour ago — verified, not assumed

PR #6187 (card #6160) changed the contract at 00:0xZ: the `merge_group` floor now **derives** from `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, so any workflow producing a required context must subscribe or the new assertion reds. This PR is the first new gate written since. I checked all three legs on the branch:

- `vi-mock-specifiers.yml` subscribes **`merge_group: types: [checks_requested]`** ✓
- Added to **`REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`** in `dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` ✓
- The `MUST_SUBSCRIBE_MERGE_GROUP` entry carries **only the reason** — *"`scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` already classifies it as a required context"* ✓

That last one is the post-#6187 shape exactly: the map carries the *reason*, the membership *derives*. An hour-old contract being followed by an author who was not told about it, because the file now explains itself, is the best evidence #6187 was the right ruling.

The workflow header also records **why it is its own unfiltered workflow** rather than a step behind `ci.yml`'s needs-a-full-run switch — *"a gate that cannot see the pull request shape most likely to trip it rebuilds the hole it exists to close"* — and notes this repo has now reached that conclusion five times. Correct, and it names its siblings.

### ⭐ The anchored-count guard caught a REAL no-op — second time tonight

> a `perl -pi` whose `s///` delimiter collided with the path failed, counts stayed 2/0, and the run reported **NO-OP / readings void** instead of a false green

Had the exit code been trusted, the ablation would have "passed" against an **unmutated** tree — the gate would have appeared to catch the historical bug while never having been shown it. That is the same class that fired on #5380 an hour ago, and it is why "prove the mutation on disk, never by the editor's exit code" is not ceremony.

The ablation itself used **the real historical instance**, as ordered: `ChatDock.partialRuntimeConfig.test.tsx` mutated to the exact one-`..`-short specifier PR #5645 wrote. Baseline exit 0 → mutated exit 1 naming that file and line → restored exit 0 with an identical census.

⭐ And the discriminating half held: all three neighbours absent from the red report — `'../AiUsageIndicator'` (one level), `'../../hooks/surfaceAgent'` (two levels), and `'../../hooks'` (two levels, resolved through `index.ts`). A resolver that got depth or index-resolution wrong would have flagged those and been deleted by the first person it annoyed.

### ⚠️ My order was wrong twice, and both corrections improve the gate

1. **I said the `vi.mock(import(…))` population was zero.** It is not — there are **three live call sites** (`plugin-kanban`, `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-list`). What is genuinely zero is the intersection this gate judges: that form written with a **relative** specifier. My claim was imprecise rather than false, and I had inherited it from the card without re-deriving. The census now counts the form separately, which is better than either of us specified.

2. ⭐ **I said "walk the tracked test files." That population has a hole.** Three files carrying real call sites match no `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` suffix, and **two match no test-file convention at all** — `vitest.setup.base.ts` and `packages/plugin-map/vitest.setup.ts`. As the report puts it: *a setup file is exactly where a repo-wide mock gets written.* The walk correctly takes every tracked JS/TS source file and lets the pattern decide, while still deriving and reporting the test-named count. Had they followed my order literally, the gate would have shipped with a blind spot in the highest-value location.

### ⭐ The false positive was fixed in the gate, and counted rather than dropped

`eslint-rules/no-dynamic-import-in-test-hook.test.js:37` holds `vi.doMock('./dep')` **inside a template literal**, as a RuleTester code sample. It is correct as written — an ESLint fixture is source *text*, so `'./dep'` has no directory to be relative to and no mock to be inert.

⛔ No test file was touched. The gate learned the distinction instead, using the discriminator the language itself uses — the `vi` **token** must be code — via the shared `js-comment-mask.mjs` literal flags. That is the same masking module PR #6195 used tonight for the same class of self-reference problem.

And the part I want quoted back to this lane:

> These are **COUNTED** as 'embedded' in the census rather than silently dropped, because **an exclusion nobody can see is how a scan narrows itself into vacuity.**

### Non-vacuity, pinned deeper than I asked

I required the population to refuse to collapse. It does — and the pin runs **end-to-end through `main()`'s exit code**, not merely the scan's return value: a throwaway git repo carrying the import graph with nothing tracked exits **1** with `population COLLAPSED`, naming sources / testFiles / relative. Pinning the return value alone would have left the exit path untested, which is where a gate actually fails open.

The census was re-derived, not quoted, and it moved: test-named **1807 → 2013** of 3696 tracked sources walked; relative specifiers **577 → 675**; **unresolvable 0 → 0, unchanged.** So the card's "not a cleanup card" premise holds.

⭐ And the tier claim was **measured and corrected downward in honesty**: the card said ~1s, the real figure is **2.7s** over 3696 files — still a checkout plus one `node` call, no install, no build. Better still, the tier is confirmed *mechanically* rather than asserted: `check:pre-install-import-graph` grew from 14/13 to 15/14 steps and stayed green, which is #6148's gate certifying that this one's import graph is install-free.

Root vitest only. Full root lint, no narrowing claimed. No changeset owed per the presence gate's own verdict.
